computed_by.description: Who produced the metric VALUE. Values for the two computable metrics (REPEATABILITY, DISCRIMINATION) must be ENGINE-produced: a hand-entered number is a declaration, not a measurement, and optimisation on a hand-entered discrimination figure only optimises the wrong target faster. Optional in the shared contract so the six oil routes keep validating; the PRECISION_GREASE_DEV skill policy layer requires the ENGINE value on those two metrics.

qualification_pipeline.description: The three qualification sub-steps in their required SERIAL order. They are not three parallel declarations: repeatability answers 'is this metric computable at all from the same sample measured many times', discrimination answers 'does a qualified stand separate a Known Good from a Known Bad', and the independent new batch check re-verifies both on a FRESH batch, because building and verifying on the same data is not verification. A later sub-step without its predecessor passing is a pipeline gap, not a stronger submission. Optional in the shared contract so the six oil routes keep validating; the PRECISION_GREASE_DEV skill policy layer requires the whole pipeline, the serial order, and an ENGINE-computed repeatability/discrimination pair.

reference_material_reference.description: Reference to the Stage 4 reference-material dossier this qualification used as its discrimination ruler. Discrimination cannot be proved without physical Known Good / Known Bad objects, so a grease-route qualification names the dossier it consumed. Optional in the shared contract so the six oil routes keep validating.

pipeline_substep.description: One qualification sub-step status. status records the outcome; evidence_reference names the record that supports it; computed_by records who produced it, so a hand-entered figure can never pass as engine-computed. All three fields are optional in the shared contract because the serial order and the ENGINE requirement are enforced by the skill policy layer for the grease route only.
